body: I shall take the spec's own numbers and see whether they hang together, and in two places they do not. First, the arithmetic of runtime: SC-004 demands that 289 cases × 3 variants × N models (up to 5, i.e. 4,335 runs) complete within the 6-hour GitHub Actions limit, while US-2's independent test allows a single case 60 minutes on one model. Even at a generous 30 seconds per run, 4,335 runs is ~36 hours; the spec never states the per-run budget that would reconcile these figures, so SC-004 is asserted rather than established. Second, and more seriously, the predictor variable is not well defined. FR-001 generates variants by 'reordering valid command sequences or substituting semantically equivalent tokens', yet FR-002 computes causal depth 'from the original semantic intent of the commands, not the manipulated token string'. If commands are reordered, the dependency structure of the actual input the model sees has changed — a command whose preconditions were satisfied by an earlier turn may now be impossible — so the depth score describes a sequence the model never received. The spec also never defines the distribution over which Shannon entropy is computed (tokens? command types? per-sequence?), nor how it is normalized to the 0.0–1.0 range of US-1; entropy of a short discrete sequence is notoriously unstable, and the edge case at line 53 concedes the variants may collapse to similar entropy. Finally, excluding crashed runs as NaN (line 52) introduces survivorship bias precisely where it matters most: if high-entropy inputs crash models, dropping those points biases the correlation toward zero, weakening the very effect the project expects to find. Each of these is fixable at spec stage by stating the entropy estimator, recomputing depth on the variant as actually issued, and pre-registering a failure-as-worst-score policy.
